verdict.whatTheRulingMeans: The instrument is real and its seven findings are sound. It executes what it says it executes: I re-ran every published coverage figure and every one reproduced. Its pin design is the best in this corpus that I have measured -- 12 of 12 attacks refused and 6 of 6 legitimate advances silent, including one UNPLANNED live advance during this review. It is nonetheless held back by three defects that the freeze legislates against by name and that the file's own docstring forbids in its own words.
verdict.whyNotACCEPT: Two of the three blockers are the instrument breaking rules it states about itself. The docstring says 'never a traceback and never a finding' and 'Exit 1 is reserved for findings about the artifact'; 21 measured inputs produce an uncaught Python traceback at exit 1. Section 8's header says 'A flattering limits count is worse than none'; the published count is 13 and a measured class of 944 falsifiable positions -- including 20 digest leaves whose true values the instrument already holds -- is not among them.
verdict.whyNotREJECT: Nothing measured here falsifies a finding it publishes, nothing it asserts about the artifact is wrong, and no repair requires discarding its design. All three blockers are additive: guard the two unguarded call sites, extend the count and digest tables from hand enumeration to derivation, and scope the finding text. A successor instrument fixes all three; none of them is a design error.
verdict.applicationDisposition: This file NARROWS RT25-RES-01 and does not close it. The artifact's own $.retainedChecker remains NONE and this instrument does not change it. A signer may read a run of this file as: the reviewed bytes are the reviewed bytes for 14 gated inputs and drift stops the run; 20 vectors, 24 invariants, the leaf census, the type sweep, the quotation scoping and the CD-RT-5 property pin were all recomputed and agree; and 7 real defects in retention-tiers.v26.json are named. definitionOfCaught.statement: A mutation is CAUGHT if and only if the run over the mutated input emits at least one finding string that is ABSENT from the baseline finding set. The exit code was never used, because the baseline is already red at exit 1 and every mutation therefore exits 1; scoring by exit code would have returned 100% on every sweep below and measured nothing.
definitionOfCaught.note: This is the same discipline the instrument applies to itself. selftest() at line 5129 computes `new = [f for f in findings if f not in base]` and requires `any(f.startswith(expected) for f in new)` -- so a mutation caught only by a DIFFERENT family is scored an escape for its own family. That is stricter than the definition I used, and it is correct.

derivedOrListed.question: Section 7.10's rider records a sibling instrument implementing the same asymmetry as `if name in UNSATISFIABLE_PINS`, a one-entry literal, which section 7.9's 'standing is DISCOVERED, not listed' forbids. Does this one derive its classes or list them?
derivedOrListed.answer: MIXED, and the mix is exactly where the value is. GATED and ADVANCING are Python literals AND ARE CROSS-COMPARED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS against the artifact's own gate strings on every run (check_recorded_inputs, lines 3598-3639). A row the artifact gates and the instrument does not is a finding; a row the instrument gates and the artifact does not is a finding; a digest mismatch between the two records is a finding. Attack A11 and A12 confirm both directions fire. That satisfies 'discovered, not listed' in substance: the literal is a transcription that cannot silently disagree with its source.

theThirdDefect.question: Section 7.2.2 records a later referent-scoped sweep finding a third defect in retention-tiers.v26.json that both the artifact's reviewer and a key-name sweep missed: $.corpusResiduals[2].measuredBoundary says 'against 18 explicitly named as unchanged' while its own sibling value says 14, and 14 is right. Does this instrument share that defect?
theThirdDefect.answer: YES. IT DOES NOT FIND IT.
theThirdDefect.verification: I confirmed the defect independently on the live bytes. $.corpusResiduals[2].measuredValues.partBSurfacesLeftUnchanged is 14. $.inheritance.exhaustivePartitionOfV24.partB holds 16 rows, of which 14 are disposition UNCHANGED and 2 are CHANGED. So 14 is right and the prose's 18 is wrong -- 18 is $.inheritance.surfacesExplicitlyUnchangedCount, a figure with a DIFFERENT REFERENT (all surfaces, not Part B surfaces). The baseline run of the instrument emits no finding at that position.
theThirdDefect.mechanism: check_counts compares exactly one prose sentence in the entire artifact, and it is hard-coded: `boundary = get_path(doc, '$.corpusResiduals[0].measuredBoundary')` with the literal regex `(\d+) inputs recorded`. corpusResiduals[1], [2] and [3] have measuredBoundary sentences and none is read. The instrument found the first defect because the author put that one path in the table by hand, and missed the mirror defect because nobody put the other one in.
theThirdDefect.soTheShapeIsNotIDENTICALToTheReviewerS: The subject's reviewer scoped by KEY NAME ('every integer leaf whose key ends in count') and could not reach a leaf called recordedInputs. This instrument does not scope by key name -- _self_referential_counts pairs a DECLARED PATH with a RECOMPUTED REFERENT, which is the right method. It scopes by ENUMERATION: the table has 29 rows, hand-written, and every self-measurement outside those 29 rows is unchecked. The failure mode is different and the blast radius is larger, because a key-name sweep at least grows automatically when a new *Count key is added, and a hand table does not grow at all.

blockers.title: AN UNREADABLE INPUT CRASHES WITH A TRACEBACK AT EXIT 1 -- THE EXIT CODE THE FILE RESERVES FOR FINDINGS ABOUT THE ARTIFACT. 21 MEASURED SITES.
blockers.rule: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE section 7.8.1 rule 3: 'An exit code a document CLAIMS must be the exit code the file PRODUCES. An instrument that misreports its own exit code is lying in the one channel a CI system reads.' Litmus D-6: 'a crash looks like a failure looks like a finding.'
blockers.measured: chmod 000 on any one of the 20 declared inputs: uncaught PermissionError, empty stdout, exit 1. 20 of 20. Plus a subject with any dotted JSON key: uncaught KeyError from hostile_sweep -> set_path, empty stdout, exit 1; reproduced with retention-tiers.v27.json's real bytes.
blockers.whyItIsBlockingAndNotPedantry: The file's OWN docstring makes this promise twice, in its own words: 'A missing input is RT26-INPUT-MISSING at exit 2, naming the path -- NEVER A TRACEBACK AND NEVER A FINDING' and 'Every failure above exits 2 with a named diagnostic whose text says the check did not run. Exit 1 is reserved for findings about the artifact.' A verdict that binds an environment (section 7.2) must hold in that environment; a read-only or root-owned artifact directory is an ordinary CI condition, not an attack.
blockers.cause: verified_inputs() lines 452-458 and 470-476 test path.is_file() and then call path.read_bytes() with no guard. check_freeze_anchors line 4387 calls read_text() the same way. main() calls type_findings() and hostile_sweep() outside every try/except; run_all()'s per-driver guard does not extend to them.
blockers.repairShape: Wrap the reads in verified_inputs, _verbatim_sources, check_freeze_anchors and main's subject read in try/except OSError -> PinRefused, so an unreadable input takes the same exit-2 path as a missing one. Wrap main's type_findings/hostile_sweep/_banner calls the way run_all wraps its drivers, and give the wrapper a distinct RT26-SWEEP-REFUSED code at exit 2 rather than a finding. Both are additive and neither touches a measurement.
blockers.notRepairableInPlace: Section 7.2 forbids editing these bytes once reviewed. The repair is check-retention-custody-v27.py.

Eight of the sharpest applied SIMULTANEOUSLY -- every predecessor digest in $.inheritance, the derivation's predecessorSha256, the v25 review digest, both encoder-control goldens, both encoder-control agree flags, and a falsified self-measurement -- produce a finding set BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE BASELINE at exit 1.
blockers.whyThisIsAFOURTEENTHAndNotAReReport: Residual 1 is scoped to prose ('every `why`, `argument`, `rationale`, `whyItMatters` and `statedCost`') and expressly excludes anything 'bound to a measurable source'. A sha256 is bound to a measurable source. Residual 8 is about a wrong TYPE rule, not a wrong VALUE. Residual 11 is about quotations OUTSIDE *Verbatim fields. Residual 13 is a blanket admission that another class probably exists -- honest, and not a limits entry.
blockers.theCorpusHasAlreadyPaidForThis: Section 7.8 records the identical defect measured on check-delivery-v4.py -- 'a recordedInputs digest replaced by 64 f's, which launders itself through the accountability gate' -- and closed in check-delivery-v5.py. It is live here at 20 positions. Section 7.6's thesis, observed from the inside: a repair confined to one lineage does not propagate.
blockers.sharpestSubCase: check_exception_set_closure COMPUTES step1 (posture-sensitive fields) and step2 (fields differing absent vs present-durable) and derives step3 = step2 - step1. It emits two of the seven baseline findings out of exactly that derivation. It never compares any of the three to the artifact's published step1/step2/step3 .count values, all three of which accept 9999 in silence. That is B-VER9R-01's shape (section 7.2.2): the evidence was gathered and then not used.
blockers.repairShape: Three moves, all additive. (1) Every string leaf matching ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ or ^(rpol1|rbnd1|sha256): is a RECORDED DIGEST; walk them and compare each against the digest table the instrument already builds, keyed by the nearest path/name sibling -- discovered, not listed. (2) Replace the 29-row _self_referential_counts table with a walk that pairs each figure to a referent, and at minimum extend the single hard-coded prose regex to every measuredBoundary in the document. (3) Compare the step1/step2/step3 counts and the encoderControl agree flags to the values the instrument has already computed.
blockers.whatThisDoesNotSay: It does not say the instrument's own findings are wrong -- they are right. It says the number 13 is not the boundary and that the file's own standard for a limits count is not met by it.

blockers.title: A CORRUPTED CITED-NOT-GATED INPUT EMITS SUBSTANTIVE FINDINGS AGAINST THE SUBJECT, AND TWO OF THEM CARRY A CLAUSE THAT IS FALSE BY CONSTRUCTION.
blockers.rule: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE section 7.8.1: 'the absence of an input became a positive, specific, plausible accusation about a completely different artifact.' Rule 2: 'Refusal must be SCOPED and NAMED.'
blockers.measured: Emptying IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md: 7 new findings, 1 naming the input (RT26-ANCHOR), 3 accusing retention-tiers.v26.json of misquotation with the false gloss 'a misquotation a predecessor already carried', 2 accusing its quotation counts, and 1 flipping a published property claim to its opposite. Replacing artifacts/product-dispositions.v1.json with {}: 12 new findings, 1 naming the input, 11 accusing the subject. Truncating the freeze by half is the worst case: 4 new findings, of which the input-naming one ('6 of 11 anchors absent') reads exactly like an ordinary legitimate edit.
blockers.theFalseClause: Both RT26-COUNT findings that fire in these cases end with 'this is a measurement about the artifact's own contents, WHICH CAN NEVER LEGITIMATELY ADVANCE'. $.quotationDiscipline.verifiedAgainstTheirAttributedSource and .notFoundInTheirAttributedSource are computed against five LIVE external files, three of which this instrument classifies ADVANCING and calls files under concurrent edit. _self_referential_counts's own docstring excludes tree-facts from that table for exactly this reason; two of its 29 rows are tree-facts.
blockers.notHostileOnly: This fires on a LEGITIMATE freeze advance that rewords any of the three freeze-attributed quotations. The freeze moved twice during retention-tiers.v26.json's own authoring by the artifact's own record, and it moved again during this review. This is section 7.10's failure mode -- a measurement of a moment dressed as an invariant -- inside the count table of the instrument written to implement section 7.10.
blockers.mitigationsIAmCreditingHonestly: Unlike the sibling instrument section 7.8.1 records, this one does say something: RT26-ANCHOR names the freeze, RT26-CDRT5 names a deleted packet row, and RT26-PIN-ADVANCED prints in the banner above every finding. That is real and it is why this is a blocker rather than the same blocker.
blockers.repairShape: Reclassify the two quotation-count rows out of the self-measurement table into the notice channel where the docstring already says tree-facts belong; and gate the RT26-B4 and RT26-COUNT quotation families on the source having been readable and non-degenerate -- if the attributed source is empty or the anchors are absent, SKIP those classes by name at a distinct code rather than reporting them, which is the named-skip shape section 7.8.1 rule 2 prescribes.

nonBlockingObservations.title: DESTROYED_PINS is a one-entry Python literal, derived from nothing, and the artifact supplies enough to derive it.
nonBlockingObservations.detail: GATED and ADVANCING are cross-compared against the artifact's own gate strings in both directions on every run. DESTROYED is not compared against anything. Section 7.10's rider names this exact shape as forbidden: 'the asymmetry is not derived at all -- it is `if name in UNSATISFIABLE_PINS`, a one-entry literal, which section 7.9's standing-is-discovered-not-listed forbids.' The artifact carries the dead digest at $.productAuthorityBoundary.amendmentDraft.itsPinHistoryIsBrokenAndThatIsRecordedRatherThanRepaired.whatHappened and the file's role at $.recordedInputs.recorded[18].role, so the classification was derivable.
nonBlockingObservations.secondDeadDigest: The same artifact field records that the v25 review measured the draft at 872c67be307866a645d246104a61065d1ab6c6d812618e0a40bbd837c4b0edb0 -- a SECOND unrecoverable intermediate state. DESTROYED_PINS carries only 4bbcd6fa.... A file reappearing at 872c67be... would be welcomed, not refused.
nonBlockingObservations.whatIVerified: The SUBSTANCE of the classification is right and I measured it against the recovery point rather than accepting it: `git show 7cc0f8a:artifacts/product-dispositions.cd-rt-5-amendment.draft.v1.json` returns nothing, so the file is genuinely absent from the 521-file recovery commit and both digests are genuinely unrecoverable. Section 7.10 rule 3 satisfied.

nonBlockingObservations.title: check_exception_set_closure takes its oracle out of the subject it is checking, which Section 1 of the same file forbids in its own words.
nonBlockingObservations.detail: Line 4087: `exceptions = set((exception_block.get('step3_theExceptionSetIsStep2MinusStep1') or {}).get('measured') or [])`, with the instrument's own derivation used only as a FALLBACK when that list is empty. Section 1's header states: 'Re-implemented here from the artifact's own published text, never imported from it and never read out of it: an instrument that reads its answers out of the artifact it is checking measures nothing.'
nonBlockingObservations.exploitability: Widening $.partA...step3...measured to the full posture-sensitive set SUPPRESSES both of the instrument's headline RT26-N01 findings. It is caught -- by a different family, RT26-A-INV-17, which compares the published step lists against the pinned v24 cells -- so this is a non-blocking defence-in-depth gap rather than an escape. But the artifact controls the input to a check about itself, and the finding it suppresses is one of the two the instrument exists to mechanise.
nonBlockingObservations.repair: Derive the exception set unconditionally and compare the artifact's published set to it, rather than preferring the artifact's.

nonBlockingObservations.title: get_path/set_path have an unescapable path grammar: no JSON key may contain '.' or '['.
nonBlockingObservations.detail: _walk_path_keys splits on '.' with no escaping. Measured on the subject: retention-tiers.v26.json has ZERO such keys and all 2935 scalar-leaf paths round-trip exactly, so no published figure is affected. Measured on the live successor: retention-tiers.v27.json has 112 dotted keys and 564 leaf paths that do not round-trip. This is CMP-IR-01's class -- a grammar to misparse -- and section 7.3's rider records array-token paths being adopted elsewhere in this corpus specifically to escape it. It is the mechanism behind IR-RTC26-B1 case 2.
nonBlockingObservations.whyOnlyNonBlocking: On these bytes it is latent, and I verified that rather than assuming it.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The 29-row count table and the 160-case mutation suite are both hand enumerations, and their gaps are visible in each other.
nonBlockingObservations.detail: The suite mutates $.recordedInputs.recorded[0].sha256 and $.theCompanionInstrumentForThePredecessor.sha256 -- two digest positions -- and 160/160 is a true statement about the 160 the author aimed. The value sweep shows what the aim did not cover: 20 other digest positions, 480 int/bool positions and the corpusResiduals[2] prose. A suite that enumerates its own targets measures the author's attention, not the surface.

nonBlockingObservations.title: SUBJECT_SHA256 is a notice, not a gate -- correctly, and with one consequence worth stating.
nonBlockingObservations.detail: A subject that is not the reviewed bytes runs to completion and prints 'N finding(s) in retention-tiers.v26.json'. Replacing the subject with {} yields 152 such findings at exit 1. The RT26-SUBJECT-MOVED notice does fire and does say the independent verdict does not cover these bytes, which is the honest half. I grade the choice CORRECT -- refusing would hide every other finding behind one line, and the docstring says so -- but a reader who greps for 'finding(s) in' and not for the notice gets 152 findings attributed to an artifact that is not there.

nonBlockingObservations.title: A quotation is verified by CONTAINMENT in its attributed source, so any true sentence from that source passes at any *Verbatim position.
nonBlockingObservations.detail: Replacing $.inheritance.section72Position.ruleVerbatim with a different genuine freeze sentence produces 0 new findings. Residual 2 covers appending a reversal to a required needle; substitution of one true quotation for another is adjacent and is not named. The scoping-by-attributed-source design is a real advance over a union search and I record it as such -- the instrument catches the INHERITED misquotation case that defeated the predecessor -- but containment cannot bind WHICH passage a field quotes.

nonBlockingObservations.title: _KEY_RENDERING captures the quoted VALUE as group 2 and never reads it.
nonBlockingObservations.detail: Line 4187: `^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*): (true|false|null|-?\d+|\".*\")$`. The list-valued Verbatim branch checks only that group 1 -- the key NAME -- exists in the pinned v24. 'closingTheDialogIsNotAnAnswer: false' therefore passes while v24 holds true. The value is parsed and discarded, at the one position where the instrument has the pinned predecessor in memory and could compare.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The PASS line does not name the --part scope.
nonBlockingObservations.detail: The banner prints 'part=a' but the green line reads 'retention-tiers.v26.json: PASS (architecture-candidate scope; CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED; ...)' with no mention of which parts ran. Measured: --part a reports 6 findings, --part c 4, --part d 3, --part all 7 (the 'all'-scope drivers run in every part, so these do not partition). On these bytes every part exits 1, so nothing is hidden today; on a successor where only Part C were red, --part a would print PASS.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The instrument's own seven findings are all sound, and two of them are genuinely new.
nonBlockingObservations.detail: I adjudicated each. RT26-COUNT x2 (recordedInputs 15 vs 19, and the sibling prose) are true and I confirmed both independently. RT26-B4-CENSUS (38 *verbatim keys vs 37 declared, the one outside being list-valued) is true and I reconciled my own first walk against it -- my count was wrong, the instrument's was right. RT26-B1-SCOPE, RT26-A and RT26-N01 x2 are internally consistent with the artifact's bytes and with the pinned v24. Nothing here is tuned and nothing is padded.

gradingTheHardCodedSUBJECT.question: SUBJECT = 'retention-tiers.v26.json' is a module constant. Is hard-coding the subject right, given it forces a new instrument per artifact version, while a subject-selection option is a surface?
gradingTheHardCodedSUBJECT.ruling: RIGHT, AND FOR A STRONGER REASON THAN THE ONE USUALLY GIVEN.
gradingTheHardCodedSUBJECT.whatIVerified: Passing 'retention-tiers.v27.json' or '--subject retention-tiers.v27.json' on the command line is refused at exit 2 with RT26-UNSUPPORTED-INVOCATION and THE CHECK DID NOT RUN. I record honestly that this is NOT a subject-selection check: it is the generic unknown-option branch, which refuses every positional argument and every unrecognised flag. There is no subject option to defeat because there is no subject option.
gradingTheHardCodedSUBJECT.whyItIsRight: Not because a flag is a surface -- a flag is a small surface. Because THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT SEPARABLE FROM ITS SUBJECT. Its 20 vector ids and 24 invariant ids are frozen tuples that must equal the artifact's ids in order; its 251 INT_LEAF_NAMES and 171 BOOL_LEAF_NAMES are transcribed from these bytes; its 29-row count table names paths that exist only in this document; its census expects exactly 1 float and 6 nulls at named paths; its 160 mutations target positions by literal path. A --subject flag would let all of that run against a document it does not describe and report the result as a measurement. Section 7.2 already says a verdict binds bytes; an instrument that accepts any subject invites a verdict that binds none.
gradingTheHardCodedSUBJECT.theCostIsRealAndIsPaidCorrectly: Section 7.6 measures the cost: 93 checkers, 88 pinned at current bytes, an editable surface of 4 files. Per-artifact instruments are why. But section 7.8's answer is the one that settles it -- 'a new checker is a new file and edits nothing' -- and this file exists because that route was taken. Per-version instruments are the price of a corpus where a verdict binds bytes.
gradingTheHardCodedSUBJECT.theOneThingIWouldChange: Not the constant. The FAILURE MODE when the wrong document arrives under the right name. Today that is either 152 findings 'in retention-tiers.v26.json' or, for a document with dotted keys, an uncaught traceback at exit 1 (IR-RTC26-B1). A cheap structural precondition -- a handful of top-level keys must exist, or the check refuses at exit 2 saying THE CHECK DID NOT RUN -- would convert both into the named refusal the file already knows how to write.

noCorpusArtifactNamedWhereItClaimsToDERI.result: ONE VIOLATION, AND IT IS NB-2.
noCorpusArtifactNamedWhereItClaimsToDERI.detail: Section 1 claims its reference derivations are 'Re-implemented here from the artifact's own published text, never imported from it and never read out of it.' Every Section 1 function takes explicit arguments and reads nothing from the subject -- that claim holds for Section 1. It does NOT hold one level up: check_exception_set_closure reads $.partA...step3...measured out of the subject and uses it as the exception set for the very resolution whose result it then reports as a finding, with its own derivation demoted to a fallback. Everywhere else I looked -- the census, the type sweep, the encoder, the partition, the vectors, the invariants -- the instrument recomputes and compares rather than reading.

corpusHygieneChecks.duplicateKeyRejection: VERIFIED. Every JSON input including the subject is parsed under object_pairs_hook=_pairs, which raises on any repeated key at any depth. A duplicate-key subject is refused at exit 2 RT26-PARSE-REFUSED.
corpusHygieneChecks.exitMatrixDistinctness: 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 did-not-run / 3 selftest-not-certifying. All four observed. Exit 3 is unconditional over a dirty base, which is the check-evidence-v9.py behaviour section 7.2 asks for. The matrix is violated only by IR-RTC26-B1's crash paths.

whatIDidNotCheck: WHETHER THE REFERENCE DERIVATIONS MODEL THE RIGHT THING. effective_posture, ask_performed, resolve_and_maybe_persist, effective_capability, admit_bounds and the Cap algebra were verified to EXECUTE and to drive 20 vectors and 24 invariants. I did not verify that they model what an implementer would build. This is the instrument's own residual 4 and I did not narrow it by one line.
ANY D9 DERIVATION. I did not execute check-d9-v1.14.py and did not verify a single D9 triple. The instrument's residual 5 declares this reduction in scope and I inherit it whole.

THE 160 MUTATION CASES INDIVIDUALLY. I confirmed the delta discipline in the source, confirmed 160/160, and confirmed the aim requirement (a mutation caught only by a different family is scored an escape). I did not audit whether each of the 160 targets a position worth targeting; NB-4 is what I can say about their coverage.

REACHABILITY OF ALL 294 ASSERTION SITES. 294 is a static count of emission sites that I reproduced. 160 are exercised by name by the suite and 7 fire on the live bytes. The remaining ~127 I did not prove reachable, and 'no vacuous site' is therefore NOT established by this review.

PROSE STRING LEAVES. I deliberately EXCLUDED the ~1284 prose string leaves from the value sweep, because the instrument already concedes them at residual 1. The 944 escapes I report are all at non-prose positions. The true escape surface is larger than 944 and I did not measure it.
WHETHER THE 14 GATED DIGESTS ARE THE RIGHT BYTES. I verified all 14 match the live files exactly. I did not verify that each of those files is the independently-reviewed version it is presented as.

THE SUBJECT ARTIFACT ITSELF. This is a review of an instrument. I adjudicated retention-tiers.v26.json only where the instrument's seven findings required it and where the referent sweep touched it. I did not review Part A, Part C or Part D on their merits.
PORTABILITY. Everything was measured on CPython 3.14.6, darwin arm64. I did not run under 3.9, and the MIN_PYTHON guard was verified by reading, not by executing a 3.9 interpreter.
CONCURRENCY. I did not test the instrument against inputs changing mid-run, only against inputs changed between runs.

THE SUPPRESSION DIRECTION AT SCALE. My sweeps measure what can be ADDED to an artifact without being caught. I probed suppression only at NB-2 and did not sweep for mutations that REMOVE a true finding.

expectationsIWasGivenThatDIDNOTHOLD: '12 of 12 attacks caught and 5 of 5 legitimate advances silent' understates the advance half: I ran 6 constructed advances plus 1 real one, all silent. The claim is conservative, not flattering.
The v27 refusal is real but is NOT a subject check. It is the generic unknown-option branch. Any positional argument produces the same message.

'294 assertion sites, 0 vacuous' -- 294 reproduces as a static count; '0 vacuous' reproduces only in the sense that no VACUOUS guard fired on live bytes. It is not established that all 294 sites are reachable, and I say so rather than passing the figure along.
reportingTheMeasurementOverTheExpectatio.theThingIWasAskedForAndFound: The dispatch asked for a fourteenth way to pass on a wrong artifact and said today's pattern was an instrument publishing four residuals against a measured 19 escapes in 30 attempts. This instrument publishes 13, and 13 is a serious, self-critical, worked list -- residual 8 and residual 13 in particular are the marks of an author who was not flattering himself. The measured answer is nonetheless 944 escapes in 1644 attempts at non-prose positions, and the fourteenth is a class rather than an instance: every recorded digest and every self-measurement outside three hand-written tables. Twenty of those are sha256 leaves whose true values the instrument is holding in memory when it declines to check them.
reportingTheMeasurementOverTheExpectatio.theThingIWasWarnedAboutAndConfirmed: Section 7.2.2's newest rider says a sweep scoped by KEY NAME cannot reach a figure whose key is not named like a count, and asks whether this instrument shares that defect. It does not scope by key name -- it pairs declared paths with recomputed referents, which is the right method. It scopes by HAND ENUMERATION instead, and the hole is in the same place: $.corpusResiduals[2].measuredBoundary says 18 where its own sibling says 14, and this instrument is silent. The lesson generalises past both: a table you write by hand and a sweep you scope by name fail on the same figure, for different reasons, and only a walk that enumerates by REFERENT reaches it.
